# Differences from MSX-AUDIO BASIC Extension Lite

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../diff-from-lite.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

For those who have used MSX-AUDIO BASIC Extension Lite (hereafter Lite), this document summarizes only the differences in Makoto BASIC Extension. Anything not described here is the same. The full specification is in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

## Sound chips

| | Lite | Makoto BASIC Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Chip | Y8950 (MSX-AUDIO), the Y8960's OPL2EX | YM2608 (Makoto), YMF288 (Misato) |
| I/O ports | `C0H`-`C1H` | `14H`-`17H` |
| FM | 9 voices (6 voices when the rhythm sounds are used) | 6 voices. Not reduced when the rhythm sounds are used |
| Rhythm | 5 instruments. Uses FM channels 7-9 | 6 instruments (the rimshot is added). Sounds built into the chip |
| ADPCM | 1 voice, up to 49716Hz | 1 voice, up to 55555Hz. Misato has none, and anything involving ADPCM is refused ([Misato](basic-reference.md#misato)) |
| SSG | None | 3 voices. The strings for SSG in the PLAY statement |
| PSG strings | The internal PSG (also SSGS in the Y8960 cartridge build) | The internal PSG |

## Statements

| | Lite | Makoto BASIC Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Initialization | `CALL AUDIO` | `CALL MAKOTO`. The arguments have the same meaning |
| Total number of channels in the PLAY statement | Up to 9 without rhythm, up to 6 with rhythm | Up to 6, with or without rhythm |
| Memory allocated | 2051 bytes (1328 bytes in the Y8960 cartridge build) | 1443 bytes (including 11 user voices) |
| `PLAY#1` | `Illegal function call` (PSG and the second set of SSGS in the Y8960 cartridge build) | SSG and PSG |
| `PLAY#2` | FM, PCM, rhythm, PSG | FM, PCM, rhythm, SSG. PSG is not played |
| `PLAY#3` | Same as `#2` (the Y8960 cartridge build adds the second set of SSGS) | FM, PCM, rhythm, SSG, PSG |
| `CALL PLAY` string numbers | Up to the number of strings +3 (+6 in the Y8960 cartridge build) | Up to the number of strings +6 (the 3 for SSG come before PSG) |
| `CALL AUDREG` register numbers | 8 bits | 9 bits (`100H`-`1FFH` are the second bank) |
| `CALL VOICE` arguments | Up to 9 | Up to 6 |
| Voice numbers | 0-95. 63 and 64-95 are user voices | 0-79. 0-68 are presets, 69-79 are user voices |
| When user voices are reset | 64-95 return to Silence at every `CALL AUDIO` | At the first `CALL MAKOTO` they become voices in which no operator sounds, and they remain until `CALL MAKOTO(-1)` |
| Voice array | 32 bytes (the layout of the Y8950 registers) | The N88-BASIC(86) voice array (50 integers) with SSG-EG and AMS added |
| `CALL VOICE COPY` destination | Numbers 63-95 | Numbers 69-79 |
| `CALL SET PCM` sampling frequency | 1800-49716 | 1800-55555 |
| `CALL MUSIC` / `CALL MINIT` / `CALL OPM` / `CALL MIDI` / `CALL MIXER` | In the Y8960 cartridge build | None |

**The contents of the voice library are different.** Even with the same number, the voice is different. The list is in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#voice-library).

**The voice array format is different.** Voice arrays made for Lite cannot be used as they are.

## MML

| | Lite | Makoto BASIC Extension |
|---|---|---|
| FM `In` | Panning (0-255, 128 is the center). Takes effect only on the Y8960's OPL2EX; does not work on the Y8950 | Panpot. `I1` left, `I2` right, `I3` both, `I0` silent |
| PCM `In` | ADPCM panning. The values and the conditions for taking effect are the same as for FM | Panpot. The values are the same as for FM |
| Rhythm `In` | Panning of channels 7-9. The values and the conditions for taking effect are the same as for FM | Panpot for all 6 instruments together. The values are the same as for FM |
| PSG `In` | SSGS panpot (0-255). Takes effect only in the Y8960 cartridge build | Accepts 0-15 and does nothing. The same for SSG |
| Rhythm instruments | `B` `S` `M` `C` `H` | Plus `F` (rimshot) |
| FM `@n` | 0-95 | 0-79 |
| PSG `N0` | Rest | Not defined. Write rests with `R`. The same for SSG |
| r of `Yr,d` | 8 bits | 9 bits. In hexadecimal, up to 3 digits can be written, as in `$1B4` |
| Registers on which m of `Yr,d,m` takes effect | `B0H`-`B8H` and `BDH` | SSG (`000H`-`00DH`), FB/AL and pan (`0B0H`-`0B2H`, `0B4H`-`0B6H`, `1B0H`-`1B2H`, `1B4H`-`1B6H`) |

The pitch is the same. FM `O4A` is 220Hz in both.

## Ticking note lengths with the timer

bit2 of the `CALL MAKOTO` mode works the same as in Lite's `CALL AUDIO`, and the tick rate is also nearly the same (about 102Hz at T32, about 204Hz at T255). The ticks come from timer A of the YM2608 (the YMF288 on Misato).

**It is assumed that the sound chip's interrupt reaches the MSX computer.**
